title: Costing, margin and break-even workings
summary: Worked numbers for your costs and prices. Recipe or product costs, profit per product, order or job, break-even, rates, price calendars and what a customer is worth.
deliverable: A worked sheet with every input shown and each formula written out: full cost, price, margin, break-even, target price or rate, or profit by product, order or job. Plus what moves the numbers, three to five actions tied to the figures, and the gaps in your data.

Break-even, discount or price change check
Labour, overhead, day or hourly rate

baseline_prompt: You are a small-business cost accountant. Using only the figures I give below, build the costing workings I ask for: recipe or product cost, profit by product, order or job, break-even, a target price or rate, or a cost comparison. Put every input in a table, write out each formula, and work out full cost, price, margin percent (profit divided by price) and break-even where they apply. Where I give sales data, rank items by profit and mark each keep, fix or cut. Label any assumption and do not invent supplier prices, wages, fees or sales numbers. Check your sums. End with three to five actions tied to the numbers and a list of gaps in my data. This is not tax or investment advice.
not_for: Tax, legal or audit advice, or any other regulated financial advice
Investment advice, or valuing a business
Agreeing prices with competitors (price-fixing)
Guarantees of profit or sales
Looking up supplier prices, duty rates or wages for you; we use only the figures you give
Bank logins, card numbers or live access to your till or accounts
A full cash flow forecast or budget (see the cash flow forecast and annual budget jobs)

sample_briefs.text: We run Hartley's Kitchen, a 40-seat cafe in Bristol. I need costed recipe cards for our 8 brunch dishes and menu prices that hit a 30% food cost, rounded up to the nearest 50p. Menu prices include VAT at 20%. Recipes and supplier prices are pasted below, for example eggs £3.10 for 15, sourdough £3.40 a loaf (14 slices), smoked salmon £28 per kg, avocados 95p each. Flag any dish where the new price looks out of line with the rest.

Ridgeway Joinery, 5 staff. Please do a profit report for the 14 jobs we finished from July to September. For each job I have the quoted price, labour hours, materials and subcontractor costs (table below). Labour costs us £24 an hour all in. Overheads are £6,200 a month and we work about 700 hours a month. Rank the jobs best to worst and tell me which kinds of job lose money.

Online candle shop, Wick & Wax. Average order £38 with 2.1 candles. Each candle costs us £6.20, packaging £1.10 per order, we pay £3.95 shipping, Shopify fees are 2% plus 25p. We get about 420 orders a month. I am planning 25% off sitewide for Black Friday. How many extra orders do I need to break even on the discount, and would a free gift on orders over £50 cost less?

Two-bed holiday let in Whitby. Mortgage £780 a month, council tax £160 a month, utilities £210 a month, insurance £540 a year, cleaning £45 per stay, average stay 3 nights, Airbnb host fee 15%. I want £12,000 profit a year. What is my break-even occupancy at £130 a night, and what nightly rate do I need at 60% occupancy?

I am a freelance bookkeeper going full time. Income goal $70,000 a year before tax. Costs: software $1,800 a year, insurance $650 a year, laptop $1,200 every 3 years, phone $60 a month. I take 6 weeks off and can bill about 24 hours a week. Work out my minimum hourly rate, a target hourly rate with a 20% buffer, and a day rate for 7 hours.

SaaS for dog groomers with three plans: $19, $39 and $79 a month. Hosting and support cost per account is $4, $9 and $22 a month. Ads cost $3,000 a month and bring 60 trial sign-ups, of which 40% go paid, split 50/35/15 across the plans. Monthly churn is 4%. Work out cost to win a paying customer, payback months and lifetime value per plan, and flag any plan that loses money.

demand_sources.note: TouchBistro guide on costing out restaurant recipes: owners cost each dish per serving to set prices that protect margin and to catch supplier price rises, keeping food cost nearer 28% than 35% of the menu price.
Small business break-even guide (March 2026) on using break-even analysis to set prices, test new products and decide on hires; it notes nearly 82% of failed small businesses cite cash flow problems.

title: Scope, brief or intake form for a piece of work
summary: One document for a piece of work. A scope or change order, a kickoff or handoff sheet, a brief for a supplier or writer, or an intake form.
deliverable: The document you choose, ready to send. A scope with deliverables, exclusions, assumptions, timeline, price and change steps. A brief with goal, specs, must-haves, budget, dates and how the work will be checked. Or an intake form, script or question list grouped by stage, with who does each step, what to collect and what you cannot advise on.

rubric.pass_rule: Sentences are mostly under 25 words; each deliverable, step or question is one line or bullet; jargon is explained or swapped; there are no legal-style phrases such as 'hereinafter' or 'indemnify'.

baseline_prompt: You are an operations manager for a small business. Write the document I ask for below, ready to send. For a scope of work: deliverables, what is not included, assumptions, timeline, price and how changes are approved. For a change order: the change, its cost, its effect on time and a sign-off line. For a brief to a freelancer, writer or supplier: goal, specs and must-haves, budget, dates and how the work will be checked. For an intake form or question list: questions grouped by stage, what to collect, and a line on what we cannot advise on. Use only the prices, dates and specs I give, and put anything missing in [square brackets]. Use plain words, not legal language.
not_for: Legal contracts, terms of service or legal advice
Collecting health, money or ID details without a lawful reason you state
Medical, legal or financial advice inside intake scripts
Sending the document or chasing replies for you
Formal requests for proposals with scoring rules (see the RFP draft job)
Passwords, card numbers or logins in the brief or in the form

sample_briefs.text: Brightside Studio, a 3-person web agency. Scope of work for a 6-page website for Oak & Ivy Florists: design, build on Squarespace, light editing of their own text (we do not write copy), 2 rounds of revisions, launch by 15 March. Price $4,800, 50% up front and 50% at launch. Not included: logo, photos, SEO beyond page titles. Extra work is $85 an hour, agreed in writing first.

Kitchen refit for a customer in Didsbury, agreed price £14,200. The customer now wants the boiler moved to the utility room. Our plumber quotes £1,150 extra and it adds 2 working days, so finish moves from 12 to 14 June. I need a short, polite change-order note they can sign before we start the extra work.

Small family law firm, 4 solicitors. We need a phone intake script for reception and a short web form for new enquiries. Collect: name, phone, email, the other party's name for a conflict check, whether children are involved, any court dates, and how they heard of us. Reception must not give legal advice. First meeting is £150 for 45 minutes.

We sell canvas tote bags as Harbour Goods. I need a one-page supplier brief and a quote request email for a new bag: 12oz natural cotton canvas, 38 x 42 cm, 10 cm gusset, inner pocket, 2-colour screen print on one side, target $3.20 a unit landed, first order 1,000, samples by 20 May. The reply table should ask for price at 1,000, 3,000 and 5,000 units, minimum order, lead time, sample cost and payment terms.

Content brief template for the 2 freelance writers on the Peak Physio blog. Fields: reader, goal, main message, sources to use, structure, call to action. Plus one filled example for the article 'How to warm up before a 10k run', 1,200 words, call to action: book a running assessment for $65. Writers must not make medical claims beyond our physio's notes, which I will paste.

We are choosing a new booking system for our 3 hair salons. I have pasted the sales sheets from the 3 vendors on our shortlist. Write pointed questions for each vendor on monthly price per chair, contract length, card fees, data export if we leave, support hours and set-up costs, aimed at what each sheet leaves out.

title: Test or research plan for one question
summary: A plan for one test, such as an A/B, price, demand, usability, beta or field test. It sets the guess to test, how to run it, how many people you need and how you will decide.
deliverable: The question and hypothesis; what to change and keep the same; who takes part and how to recruit; tasks or scripts; sample size and duration with the working; the right statistical test; what to measure; stop and win rules set in advance; and what you will do for each result.

spec_fields.label: What kind of test or research?
options: A/B test of a page, email, ad or store change
A short series of ad or creative tests
Test of a risky guess about a segment or idea
Usability test, tree test or card sort
Beta test or pilot, including an AI pilot
Sample size and the right statistical test only
Analysis plan for a survey or test

spec_fields.label: How many tests?
spec_fields.help: Base price covers 1 test. A four-week series of 4 ad tests counts as 4.

spec_fields.label: What do you want to learn or decide?
Your current numbers
spec_fields.help: Visitors, conversion rate, orders, list size, users or leads per week, and results so far. Needed for sample size.

spec_fields.label: What you plan to change or try
Who takes part or sees the test?
spec_fields.help: For example: new visitors only, current members, 5 pet owners.

spec_fields.label: Tools you will use
spec_fields.help: For example: Shopify app, Google Ads experiments, Zoom, a survey tool.

spec_fields.label: Smallest change worth acting on
spec_fields.help: For example: a 10% lift in sign-ups. If blank, the plan proposes one and labels it.

spec_fields.label: Survey questions or results, if any
spec_fields.help: For an analysis plan or a statistical test check.

rubric.text: The plan answers the buyer's question with a clear hypothesis and the decision it informs.
rubric.pass_rule: Each test states the question from the brief, one written hypothesis (if we change X, Y will change because Z) or a research aim for qualitative work, and the decision the result will drive. A plan with no hypothesis or aim, or no decision, fails.

rubric.text: Traffic, conversion and baseline figures come from the brief; anything assumed is labelled.
rubric.pass_rule: Every baseline number used (visitors, conversion rate, list size, orders, users, budget) appears in the brief or is labelled as an assumption with a note to replace it. Invented benchmarks, industry averages or past results fail.

rubric.text: Sample size, duration and the statistical test are worked out and fit the data.
rubric.pass_rule: For a numeric test, the draft shows the inputs (baseline, smallest change, confidence and power or the rule used), sample size per group, duration from the brief's traffic, and a test that fits the measure. Recomputed duration matches within 10%. Qualitative plans state participant numbers and why; analysis plans name the count or test for each question.

rubric.text: Complete and ready to run, with rules set before launch.
rubric.pass_rule: The draft lists the versions or tasks, what stays the same, the main measure and up to two guard measures, a stop rule and a win rule written before launch, and what to do for each result (win, lose, no clear result). Usability and field plans include the script or tasks in full.

rubric.text: Plain words: a busy owner can run it without a statistics background.
rubric.pass_rule: Each statistical term (such as significance, power or confidence) is explained in one plain sentence; steps are numbered; sentences are mostly under 25 words; no result or lift is promised.

baseline_prompt: You are a research and experimentation lead for small businesses. Write a test plan for the question below. Give the question, one hypothesis, what to change and what to keep the same, who takes part and how to recruit them, the tasks or script if people are involved, the main measure and guard measures, the sample size per group and how long to run it with the working shown from my traffic, the statistical test to use, and stop and win rules decided before launch. Say what I should do if it wins, loses or shows no clear result. Use only my numbers and label any assumption. Explain any statistics term in plain words. Do not promise a result.
not_for: Running the test, setting up tools or reading live dashboards for you
Tests that deceive, harm or pressure people
Medical, clinical or drug trials, or research that needs ethics approval
Guaranteed results or a promised lift
Legal advice on pricing or consumer rules
Ranking a long list of test ideas (each plan covers named tests)
Passwords or logins to your tools

sample_briefs.text: Fernhill Coffee Roasters online shop: about 18,000 visitors a month and 2.1% of visitors buy. I want to test a new product page that shows the subscription option first. We use Shopify with the Shoplift testing app. What sample size do we need, how long should it run, and what should we watch so we do not hurt average order value ($31 now)?

Our yoga app charges $9.99 a month. We get about 1,400 new trials a month and 38% become paying members. I want to test $12.99 for new trials only, without upsetting current members. Plan the test: who sees which price, how long, what to measure, and when to stop or roll back.

We built a new online booking flow for Little Paws Dog Daycare. Plan a usability test with 5 dog owners over Zoom: goals, who to recruit and how, 5 tasks, a session script, follow-up questions and what counts as a pass for each task.

Thinking of selling a meal-prep kit for climbers. No product yet. I have £300 for Instagram ads over one week and can build a simple landing page in Carrd. Plan a fake-door demand test: the page outline, the main message, the success number set in advance, and what we do on each result.

Four-week plan of Meta ad tests for our roofing company in Leeds. Budget £1,200 in total. We get about 40 leads a month at £28 each. I want to test the hook, the image type, the offer and form length, one at a time. Give the calendar, budget per version, stop rule and a simple scoreboard.

We sent two subject lines to 3,000 subscribers each. A: 24% opened and 2.8% clicked. B: 27% opened and 3.1% clicked. Which statistical test should I use to check whether B really won on clicks, and how big would each group need to be next time to spot a 0.5 point difference in click rate?

30-day AI pilot for our 6-person accountancy practice. We want to try AI for drafting client emails and for summarising bank statements. Plan how to measure time and quality before and after, who takes part, and a go or stop rule. Staff currently spend about 6 hours a week on client emails.
